title: WHAT NORM LEARNS
note: Single-source ADN feature. Norm is a labelled metaphor for the learn-normal mechanism the three projects are described as using. No project is shown launched, live, deployed or piloted.

lines.text: Press a blob against a boot, and it remembers the boot.
lines.t: Press a blob against a boot, and it remembers the boot.

lines.text: Meet Norm, a blob standing in for a machine that learns normal. Press the real boot back, and anywhere it doesn't fit, he glows red.
lines.t: Meet Norm, a blob standing in for a machine that learns normal. Press the real boot back, and anywhere it doesn't fit, he glows red.

lines.text: Three University of Alaska projects, shown at a statewide A I symposium, each start from one particular thing.
lines.t: Three University of Alaska projects, shown at a statewide A I symposium, each start from one particular thing.

lines.text: First, a ski turn. Jan Ronner, a former U A A alpine racer, is building FlowLine, an A I app that grades a skier's uploaded video and suggests drills.
lines.t: First, a ski turn. Jan Ronner, a former U A A alpine racer, is building FlowLine, an A I app that grades a skier's uploaded video and suggests drills.

lines.text: Online advice, Ronner said, is very generic.
lines.t: Online advice, Ronner said, is very generic.

lines.text: So picture Norm pressed with one skier's turn. Ronner plans to launch in December.
lines.t: So picture Norm pressed with one skier's turn. Ronner plans to launch in December.

lines.text: Second, a kitchen. Nathan Healy presented ANCHOR, built to help older Alaskans stay independent.
lines.t: Second, a kitchen. Nathan Healy presented ANCHOR, built to help older Alaskans stay independent.

lines.text: Motion sensors and one button learn a senior's routines, and it's designed to alert family when a routine slips past a safety threshold.
lines.t: Motion sensors and one button learn a senior's routines, and it's designed to alert family when a routine slips past a safety threshold.

lines.text: Third, a machine. Graduate student Aaron Smith uses digital twins, virtual copies of real equipment, to model compressors for a proposed gas pipeline.
lines.t: Third, a machine. Graduate student Aaron Smith uses digital twins, virtual copies of real equipment, to model compressors for a proposed gas pipeline.

lines.text: Smith calls the compressor that pipeline's heartbeat, and the Daily News reports an estimate of more than fifty four billion dollars for the pipeline.
lines.t: Smith calls the compressor that pipeline's heartbeat, and the Daily News reports an estimate of more than fifty four billion dollars for the pipeline.

lines.text: Do they work yet? That Daily News story, the only report found, names no users, no accuracy figures and no pilots.
lines.t: Do they work yet? That Daily News story, the only report found, names no users, no accuracy figures and no pilots.

lines.text: These are showcase projects, so early is fair. Proof would be a December start that holds, a first household for ANCHOR, and a twin checked against a real compressor.
lines.t: These are showcase projects, so early is fair. Proof would be a December start that holds, a first household for ANCHOR, and a twin checked against a real compressor.

lines.text: So what would you press Norm against first?
lines.t: So what would you press Norm against first?
